Your count files are at gene level, but the exam needs isoform (transcript) level counts.
Those can’t be derived from gene counts, so the reads have to be re-quantified from the raw sequencing data (FASTQ files).

#### SRA run IDs → FASTQ reads → Salmon (counts per transcript) → tximport in R → isoform and gene count matrices 

What each step does

1.  Sample list. The SRR run IDs are already in your metadata tables. They tell the download tool which sequencing runs belong to each sample.

```{r}
# The SRR run IDs are already in the metadata
# (GSE119579 and GSE158752 are the objects from the setup script)
writeLines(a$meta$Run, "runs_GSE119579.txt")
writeLines(b$meta$Run, "runs_GSE158752.txt")
```

2.  Download (sra-tools). prefetch downloads the compressed .sra file, and fasterq-dump converts it into FASTQ files. The reads are paired-end, so each sample gives two files (\_1 and \_2).

<!-- -->

1.  Build the Salmon index (once). The index is a searchable version of the reference transcriptome (GENCODE). Salmon compares each read against it.
2.  Quantify (Salmon). Salmon does not align reads to the genome. It estimates how many reads come from each transcript, which also resolves reads that match several isoforms of the same gene. It writes a quant.sf file per sample.
3.  Import into R (tximport). tximport reads all quant.sf files and builds one matrix with a row per transcript and a column per sample. This is the isoform count matrix.
4.  Gene counts. Summing the isoform counts that belong to each gene (using a transcript-to-gene table) gives the gene count matrix. Both matrices then come from the same pipeline and share the same identifiers.
5.  Metadata. The metadata rows are put in the same order as the matrix columns. This is checked with stopifnot(identical(...)).
